title: When does a neuron explanation actually work?
description: A plain-language explanation of Leo Gao’s research discussion about testing neuron explanations. The traffic-light analogy and animated diagrams are illustrations, not experimental results.

scenes.heading: A label is a hypothesis
scenes.narration: A neuron is one small computational unit inside a neural network. If it responds to a recognizable pattern, have we explained it? In a new research discussion, Leo Gao argues that a neat label is only the start.

scenes.heading: Predict beyond the examples
scenes.narration: Think of guessing traffic-light rules from a few photos. You see a red light, and the cars are stopped. Seems simple. But does your rule predict what happens in situations you haven’t seen? This is just an analogy.

scenes.heading: Two ways a label can fail
scenes.narration: Gao points to two gaps. A neuron may respond to only some examples matching its label. And activation strength means the size of its response. That strength may carry information the label ignores.

scenes.heading: Replace the response
scenes.narration: His proposed check is simulation: predict a neuron's numerical response, then replace the real response with that prediction. Does the network still behave the same way?

scenes.heading: Measure what changes
scenes.narration: One comparison uses downstream KL divergence. It measures how much the model's output probabilities change, across many inputs. A pretty explanation that changes those outputs can be missing something important.

scenes.heading: A test, not a safety guarantee
scenes.narration: This is a research argument, not a new experimental result. The metric is imperfect, and explaining individual neurons still doesn't explain the computations between them.

scenes.heading: Understand the mechanism
scenes.narration: The takeaway: use patterns to form hypotheses, then test what those hypotheses preserve. Read Leo Gao's full post, Neural networks are not already clean, for the argument and caveats.

claims.text: A plausible pattern among activating examples is not sufficient to establish that a neuron is explained.
A neuron can respond to only a subset of the situations matching a proposed label.
Activation strength may carry important information that a category label leaves unexplained.
Gao proposes predicting activations and substituting the simulated values to check whether model behavior is preserved.
Gao proposes evaluating explanations with downstream KL divergence over a large dataset.
Gao considers the KL metric imperfect; individual neuron explanations are only part of understanding the network.

limitations: This source is a research argument, not a new empirical demonstration.
Downstream KL is an imperfect test; preserving it does not establish complete understanding or general AI safety.
Understanding individual neurons does not by itself explain the computations between them.
